title: Review: Sol fourth pass over the A5 integration PR
description:
READ-ONLY REVIEW. Do not edit, create, or delete any file; do not commit; do not push. Your only writes are bd notes on this bead and closing it.

SCOPE: the full diff of branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8 against origin/main (`git diff origin/main...HEAD`) — one PR carrying eight beads: eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.4 (character suffocation recovery gate, migration 0032, set_suffocation, calc breath formulas), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.5 (player-character death rules for encounter combatants, migration 0033), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.6 (adjust_hp knockOut), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.3 (adjust_exhaustion, derived level-4 HP maximum, level-6 death), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.11.4 (expend_ammunition / recover_ammunition, migration 0034), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.10.3 (roll_retained_check / resolve_retained_check / end_retained_check, set_surprised derived from comparisons, migration 0035), eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.6 (hydra Multiple Heads curated mechanic, tracked head count, derived reaction allowance, migration 0036), eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.5 (action:use-an-object ordinaryInteractionRuleRef -> rule:other-activity-on-your-turn, importer). Run `bd show` on each bead and on eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8 for the specs and acceptance criteria.

AUTHORITY: AGENTS.md; docs/design-and-pr-review-policy.md (profile rules-clause-complete); ADR 0020 §§2-3 (dice, arithmetic, atomic state mutation, resource accounting, state integrity are deterministic; adjudicated outcomes still pass through those boundaries); docs/design/rule-record-runtime-statements.md amendments A3-A5 and invariants 12-13; ADR 0015 (migration-first schema); docs/importer-fix-protocol.md for the importer parts; the committed SRD source text for every rule (packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json, records use the `key` field).

METHOD (review the mechanism, not the narrative):
1. For each capability, print the governing SRD source text beside the implementation and check source fidelity of every engine rule (thresholds, tie semantics, rounding, ordering, what counts as damage/healing, lifecycle start/end).
2. Check every model-facing surface (tool descriptions, schemas, Hybrid Contract in protocol.ts, known-limit statements in ruleKnownLimits.ts, error/rejection messages) against the real code: truthful, no model-side arithmetic/comparison or model-held canonical state offered as a fallback, target domain correct (character vs combatant), no stale wording from the pre-capability disclosures.
3. State integrity: atomicity (single transaction), invariants across the full state space (alive/dying/stable/dead, monster vs player-character rules, recovery block, exhaustion levels, closed vs active combat instances, missing/malformed rows), concentration and attunement side effects, campaign-actor sync, provenance conventions, deterministic ids/replay, write paths that bypass established helpers (mutateState, claimItem, removeItem), migration correctness (constraints, indexes, data preservation, contiguity, schema snapshot).
4. Write paths that let a model persist an unsupported/derived value (the A5 forbidden-substitution class), and any place a refusal could be bypassed through another tool (e.g. add_condition, update_combatant status, rest, level-up).
5. Test evidence: does each acceptance criterion have a test that distinguishes the bad state from the good state? Name missing evidence only where a real requirement is unprotected.
6. Sibling search: for each defect, look for the same class elsewhere in the diff.

REPORT with `bd update <this bead> --append-notes`, then `bd close <this bead>`. One entry per finding: ID (S1, S2, ...), severity (blocker / should-fix / nit), file:line, the violated requirement and its authority, a concrete failure scenario (inputs -> wrong state), and the minimal fix. Then a short list of what you checked and found correct. Apply the review policy's "From observation to finding" test: an observation without an operative requirement is "no requirement" in one line, not a finding. Do not stop at the first defect; batch everything you can find.

FOURTH PASS. Prior Sol reviews: eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.1, .8.4, .8.6 (read all three). Repairs since .8.6: batch D eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.7 (structural lifecycle invariants I1-I8 asserted on the final state of every combatant/actor write, seeded 360-step tool-sequence invariant test, promotion lifecycle transfer, migration 0037 stable_recovery_settled, original-expenditure ammunition entitlement, resolver threading, full-damage instant death at 0 HP) and a supervisor commit correcting the suffocation known limit and set_suffocation description. (1) State CLOSED/OPEN for S3, S4, S12, S14, S19, S20, S21 with fresh adversarial evidence. (2) Attack the invariant layer itself: is assertCombatantLifecycle (or equivalent) actually reached on EVERY combatant and actor write path (grep every UPDATE/INSERT of encounter_combatant and campaign_actor), are I1-I8 correct against the source, and does the generated sequence test exercise the tools that matter? (3) Fresh full review of the rest of the PR for anything not yet found (IDs from S22). Apply "From observation to finding" strictly. Close with APPROVE-READY or CHANGES REQUESTED.
acceptance_criteria: Closure states plus any new findings recorded in bd notes with an overall disposition; no file changes; bead closed by the reviewer.

S3 | OPEN | blocker | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:2392
Requirement/authority: condition:exhaustion level-six death; eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.3; .19.3.4.8.7 S3 expressly requires terminal death to survive non-damage clamps, including base/effective maximum 1/0. ADR 0020 owns the lifecycle.
Fresh registered failures: start a 1/1 goblin, opt into player-character death rules, adjust_exhaustion(delta:6). It refuses with I1 and rolls back to alive/1 HP/exhaustion absent instead of committing dead/0 HP/exhaustion 6. irreversibleDeath initially sets dead, then the clamp branch overwrites it with dying. Sibling: mark a 1/1 PC-rules combatant dead, then exhaustion +4; the same branch changes dead to dying and I8 rejects the required clamp, leaving HP unclamped and exhaustion unchanged.
The old separate-call participation escape and supplied-HP suffocating-actor admission reproductions now correctly refuse; assertions prevent the old corrupt commit, but rejecting these required transitions does not discharge the capability.
Minimal fix: make dead/irreversible death take precedence in the zero-maximum clamp before checking the final state; commit the required exhaustion operation rather than relying on the checker to reject its own intermediate result.
Permanent evidence: generalized transition invariant across existing alive/dead, both death modes, base maxima 1/larger, and level-six/level-four clamps, asserting successful permitted operations, HP, status and conditions together. Owner: combatant/exhaustion integration. Material repair; requires fresh subsystem review.
S4 | OPEN | blocker | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:387; :1954; real producers packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts:2903, :4787
Requirement/authority: ADR 0020 canonical actor ownership/persistence; .8.7 S4 requires complete lifecycle transfer with exactly one recovery owner; SRD stable recovery and .19.5.7.5 PC parity.
Fresh registered real-producer sequences: instantiate a module goblin, opt into PC rules, link it to an until-removed summoning effect with campaignActorId durable, knock it to 0, stabilize it, and close combat. Promotion copies the deadline into actor.state.combatLifecycle but clears it from the only encounter row and marks that row settled. advance_time(240) reports zero recoveries and leaves durable stable/0 HP despite its expired deadline: recovery scans encounter_combatant only, never the newly promoted actor. Variant: stabilize BEFORE creating the owning effect; first promotion clears the source schedule, then closing combat promotes it again and overwrites the actor's deadline with null/settled:true. This permanently cancels ordinary positive-maximum recovery even after reopening.
Dying counters/suffocation and hydra current/pending head facts now survive the real producer and reopen correctly.
Minimal fix: establish an authoritative recoverable actor/projection owner during promotion; resolve that owner's deadline through the clock, and ensure repeated promotion cannot replace an owned schedule with the invalidated historical source. Settled must describe actual resolved recovery, not stand in for transferred ownership.
Permanent evidence: generalized real-producer continuity across stable before/after effect creation, closure, due time before/after reprojection and repeated promotion; assert actual regained HP plus actor/projection state. Owner: actor/clock integration. Material repair.
S12 | CLOSED | packages/core/src/rules/ruleKnownLimits.ts:153; packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolSetSuffocation.ts:27
Fresh source/surface review: the suffocating limit now identifies the concrete adjust_hp/update_combatant damage-versus-drop trap, names registered participants, and directs the valid set_suffocation operation. The tool itself correctly explains survival interval before the next-turn drop and distinguishes character/PC-rules dying from default monster death. Printed rule:suffocating and checked breath formulas and timing. Food/water/speed retired limits and retained-check wrong-tool traps remain correct. The prior positive-mapping-only defect is closed.
S14 | OPEN | should-fix | packages/core/src/state/hpLifecycle.ts:391, :914; packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:1956
Requirement/authority: .8.7 S14 accepts deliberately settled zero-regain stable state, rejects every partially null schedule, and clears settled on leaving stable; ADR 0020 state integrity; rule:temporary-hit-points permits a buffer at 0 HP without healing or waking the creature.
Fresh reachable sequence: character 1/1 -> exhaustion +4 -> stabilize -> advance_time(240). Repeated clock advances now work, fixing the original deadlock. But grant_temporary_hp(amount:5) then fails I7 and rolls back; ordinary adjust_hp(amount:1) also fails rather than returning zero regain. writeHpFields unconditionally changes stable_recovery_settled to 0 while keeping stable and the all-null schedule, then asserts the intermediate invalid state. Combatant adjustments rearm this state; the shared character writer does not.
Malformed-state sibling, intentionally seeded only to exercise the expressly required integrity refusal: after legitimate settlement, set stable_recovery_roll=1 while leaving anchor/deadline null and settled=1. advance_time succeeds for BOTH character and combatant, because the malformed-row queries exclude every settled row; .8.7 explicitly requires partial-null rejection regardless of settled.
Minimal fix: preserve a valid settled state on unrelated writes, or apply the authorized rearm before final validation; reject any partial schedule independently of settled, accepting all-null only for the valid settled form. Do not invent minimum-one HP or compulsory automatic retry.
Permanent evidence: generalized settled-state operation sequence over healing/temp-HP/exhaustion and repeated time, plus all-null versus partial-null schedules across both domains. Owner: shared HP/clock integration. Material repair. Severity reduced from the prior campaign-wide clock deadlock to should-fix for the remaining operation/integrity failures.
S19 | OPEN | should-fix | packages/core/src/state/ammunition.ts:249
Requirement/authority: .8.7 S19 and .19.5.11.4: entitlement per ammunition identity is floor(original expended quantity/2), limited by actual availability; rule:weapon-properties; ADR 0020 resource accounting.
Fresh fully registered sibling: give four identical arrows; expend two twice. Destroy the LAST drop (the original source row arrows) using supported remove_item(disposition:destroyed), close combat, recover. Result entitlement:2, recovered:1, destroyed:1, unavailable:2. Four originally expended and two present require recovered:2/destroyed:0. Destroying the FIRST split drop correctly returns two, so the repaired result depends on which physical row was destroyed. Once both the drop and source row are deleted, identity falls back to unavailable-source and is grouped separately from surviving arrows, stranding part of the original entitlement.
Minimal fix: retain immutable ammunition identity on the expenditure ledger (or an equivalent durable accounting identity); do not reconstruct it only from deletable physical inventory rows. Compute each identity's entitlement over every original expenditure and cap it by availability once.
Permanent evidence: generalized accounting invariant varying first/last/all/partial destruction, odd/even original quantities and mixed identities; assert entitlement, returned, destroyed and unavailable. Owner: ammunition integration. Material accounting repair.
S20 | OPEN | should-fix | packages/core/src/state/actionEconomy.ts:1452; packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:2573; packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts:1828
Requirement/authority: exact campaign-rules resolver boundary; .8.7 S20 requires installed-add-on parity for surprised combatant observers and combatant exhaustion; ADR 0020 selected capabilities.
Fresh registry probe with installLateAmbiguityAddon and its resolver installed on ToolContext: start_encounter succeeds; retained Stealth/passive comparison succeeds. set_surprised for an ordinary goblin observer still fails unavailable add-on: its nested combatantHeadCount call omits input.resolveRulesPack, and a null head count invokes default resolution. A tracked hydra observer succeeds because its nonnull count short-circuits that lookup.
adjust_exhaustion(delta:1) still fails for both goblin and hydra with the same available resolver. Tool/state/updateCombatant threading now exists, but updateCombatant's concentration/incapacitation condition check calls anyConditionImpliesIncapacitated without a resolver; conditionImpliesIncapacitated uses default lookup. A source-level throwaway probe confirms that exact stack. Failures roll back state.
The new set_surprised add-on test targets a CHARACTER, which bypasses combatantHeadCount; it does not protect the specified combatant observer. No add-on exhaustion regression covers the remaining helper.
Minimal fix: thread the resolver into combatantHeadCount and the condition/profile lookups participating in the exhaustion mutation, preserving exact-binding failure and rollback when genuinely unavailable.
Permanent evidence: generalized available/unavailable bound-stack consumer parity with ordinary/hydra COMBATANT observers and exhaustion, asserting successful mutation when installed and no writes otherwise. Owner: surprise/exhaustion integration. Material consumer-wiring repair.
S21 | CLOSED | packages/core/src/state/hpLifecycle.ts:645
Fresh registry matrix: start dying/stable at 0 HP/max20, grant 40 temporary HP, then damage20 with critical false/true. All four cases now correctly persist dead, instantDeath:true, buffer40->20 and no added failure, although overflow is zero. Reviewed the committed below/equal/above maximum x absent/partial/full-buffer matrix. The separate positive-HP initial drop still compares penetrating overflow. S22 | blocker | packages/core/src/state/exhaustionMutation.ts:132; packages/core/src/state/hpLifecycle.ts:422
Requirement/authority: .19.5.7.3 requires atomic level-six character death; condition:exhaustion; ADR 0020. .8.7 assertions are required on FINAL canonical state, not before necessary lifecycle work completes.
Fresh registered failure: living character20/20, exhaustion absent -> adjust_exhaustion(delta:6). The tool fails I1 and rolls back to alive20/20 with no exhaustion. It first writes level6, then clamps current HP to10; writeHpFields asserts level6 requires dead before killCharacterFromExhaustion runs. Any character that needs the level-four clamp when directly reaching six is affected, including base1/effective0. The existing cap/death test first raises to five, so its second write needs no clamp and misses this regression.
Minimal fix: combine the condition, non-damage clamp and required death/side effects into one valid transition and validate after its final state; preserve transaction rollback and concentration/attunement effects.
Permanent evidence: generalized character exhaustion-death boundary with existing levels below/above four, current HP above/at/below new maximum, zero/larger maxima and temporary buffers; assert success plus conditions/HP/death/side effects. Owner: character exhaustion/HP integration. Material repair.
S23 | should-fix | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:2434
Requirement/authority: .8.7 I8 expressly preserves ordinary monster-rules revival by healing as the one exception when neither exhaustion-six nor zero-head death caused it; .19.5.7.5 preserves default monster behavior. This explicit supervisor decision governs the exception.
Fresh registered failure: ordinary monster-rules goblin20/20 -> hpDelta:-20 -> hpDelta:+1. The second call succeeds and persists HP1/status:dead, including its durable actor. The new monster branch unconditionally preserves dead, even for the authorized ordinary-healing exception. Original/main changes this state to alive. No terminal cause is present.
Minimal fix: distinguish a non-damage/death-preserving clamp from the expressly allowed monster healing transition; derive alive for that authorized exception while preserving PC terminality and exhaustion/head death.
Permanent evidence: generalized transition boundary for ordinary versus terminal-cause monster death, heal versus clamp, and PC parity; assert status and HP together. Owner: combatant lifecycle integration. Material behavioral repair.
S24 | should-fix | packages/core/test/exhaustion.test.ts:254, :317
Requirement/authority: .8.7 explicitly requires the generated sequence to assert I1-I8 after every step and protect the lifecycle class; review policy Proof mechanisms are implementation and AGENTS Permanent Test Evidence require evidence that distinguishes bad state.
Fresh independent replay of the exact seed/360 calls: record_death_save 62 errors/0 successes; stabilize_character 64 errors/0 successes; set_suffocation 60 errors/0 successes. Low-bit correlations generate ONLY event:breathe (never drop), ONLY negative hpDelta (51 damage, no healing), and ONLY positive exhaustion delta (70 increases, no reductions). The transient lifecycle paths never execute successfully. assertState has no prior-state history, so it cannot assert I8; a dead-to-alive transition satisfying snapshot I1-I7 would pass. It also permits stable schedules with one/two present fields and omits recovery schedule/pending-head parity on reopen. Tool outcomes for these 360 calls are ignored.
Minimal fix: use state-aware operation generation or deterministic scenario mixing that reaches the selected valid transitions and both directions, check expected successes/refusals, preserve previous state for I8, enforce complete I7 and lifecycle parity. Do not increase the step count as a substitute.
Permanent evidence: this repaired generalized sequence is itself the required evidence; small coverage assertions on successful lifecycle classes and full transition/parity checks suffice. No second test of the test is required. Owner: lifecycle regression evidence. Material proof repair.
S25 | blocker | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:608; real caller packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts:3155
Requirement/authority: .8.7 requires I1/I6 on every campaign-actor lifecycle write; condition:exhaustion requires death at6 and a halved maximum at4; ADR 0020 forbids model-written canonical substitutes.
Fresh registered alternate-write probe: create an ordinary pretracking-shaped durable actor through existing upsertCampaignActor (alive20/20, state:{}), then start_effect(kind:condition-package, source:ruling, duration:until-removed) with a condition projection {target:{kind:campaign_actor,ref:legacy},condition:{id:exhaustion,level:6}}. It succeeds and commits alive20/20/exhaustion6/state:{}. Missing combatLifecycle is normal for existing actors predating this PR; migration0033 preserves their state_json. assertCampaignActorLifecycle returns before checking any invariant when that subtree is absent. Level4 has the same unchecked HP maximum boundary. This real model-facing effect path also bypasses the exhaustion refusal imposed on character/combatant addCondition.
Minimal fix: apply subtree-independent invariants such as I1/I6 regardless of whether lifecycle tracking exists, and route/refuse engine-owned exhaustion through the canonical capability on this alternate actor seam. Give unknown lifecycle facts their bounded admission/refusal rather than skipping validation.
Permanent evidence: generalized actor write/admission invariant with missing/present lifecycle and exhaustion below/at4/6 through the real effect producer; assert rejection/rollback or authorized derived state. Owner: actor/invariant integration. Material repair.
S26 | should-fix | packages/core/src/state/actionEconomy.ts:853; packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:474, :1324, :1531
Requirement/authority: .8.7 STRUCTURAL INVARIANT expressly requires final validation of EVERY combatant write, including source admission, head settlement, projection/schedule transfer. It is an accepted responsibility, not an inferred request for generic defensive programming.
Exhaustive SQL producer search finds uncovered paths: source encounter insertCombatant never calls assertCombatantLifecycle; beginTurn's bulk accumulator reset validates none of its affected rows; head settlement with no healing calls only syncCombatantActor (which neither validates the combatant nor acts on non-actor projections); old projection schedule invalidation is not followed by validation of the old rows. Checked direct UPDATE/INSERT producers in all production packages; other lifecycle mutations do reach the checker.
Fresh integrity-boundary probe: seed a schema-valid I1-invalid historical/fixture combatant row (alive20/20/exhaustion6), call registered begin_turn for the character. The bulk encounter_combatant UPDATE commits its new damage_turn_key and returns success with that written combatant still alive/exhaustion6. This is an intentionally malformed-state probe, not a claim that begin_turn itself creates exhaustion6. Current reachable consequences are lower than S25's model write; nevertheless the specified unconditional write gate is absent.
Minimal fix: validate every affected final combatant state in the owning transaction at these producers, including non-actor and historical rows, or enforce one shared transaction-level mutation seam covering them. Preserve legitimate schedule-transfer states and avoid asserting temporary intermediate states.
Permanent evidence: a small generalized invariant-boundary regression over the uncovered write families and representative invalid final states, plus the repaired valid sequence; proportional to the explicitly retained state-integrity gate. Owner: structural lifecycle integration. Material guard-coverage repair.
Checked and found correct, subject to the findings above:
- Source-grounded suffocation gates, preserved dying counters, clear-on-breathe/death, and ordinary concentration/attunement boundaries. Selected knockout consumes temporary HP, bypasses lethal overflow, enters stable, and arms seeded recovery atomically.
- Ordinary exhaustion arithmetic/caps, uniform floor halving, non-damage clamps without temp-HP/head damage, long-rest final-maximum ordering, level-up clamping and roster/detail HP projections. Exceptions are S3/S22/S25.
- Ordinary recurring actor current-projection ownership uses active projection then combat insertion order; old manual writes are refused. Reserved combatLifecycle injection/removal is refused/preserved. Real module promotion now retains dying/suffocation and current/pending hydra facts; S4 concerns deadline ownership.
- Ammunition reservations prevent claim/give bypasses and omit reserved drops from nearby discovery. Normal even/odd/mixed identity recovery, canonical custody/destruction, location/closed-battle rules, repeat-settlement refusal and second-battle reuse work. S19 remains the deleted-identity sibling.
- Retained comparisons never reroll the retained side, roll only active search, use strict observer-win ties and passive adjustments, validate campaign/participant identity, reject ended checks, and expose bounded active identities after resume. Surprise accepts comparison ids and refuses model-supplied participant lists; reaction totals are likewise closed. Ledger/trace/audit presentation consumers are wired.
- Committed Hydra curation pins five heads, one head at25 damage per turn, two regrown per lost head, fire suppression, ten HP per new head and all-head death; head-derived reaction restriction and own-turn/skipped-turn settlement are integrated. Unknown upgraded head count has truthful bounded refusal.
- Use-an-object relationship resolves to the actual free combat interaction source. Generated changes are exactly that pointer and the Multiple Heads mechanic; importer curation/source guard/schema and relationship evidence inspected.
- Migrations0032-0037 are contiguous; constraints/indexes, row preservation, fresh/adopted parity and generated snapshot evidence pass. Gap registry/validator/audit projection have explicit retained disposition and a real nonempty injected projection regression.

No requirement: unlimited retained-check enumeration beyond the accepted most-recent20 context boundary.
No requirement: generic configurable head suppression outside the positively selected committed hydra mechanic.
No requirement: automatic minimum-one effective HP or an unsolicited revival operation.
No requirement: permanent exact reproducer for every throwaway probe; findings specify proportionate generalized evidence.
